recommendation: No database for launch; Neon Launch for future SQL persistence, Firestore Blaze for a document model if threshold billing is acceptable.

providers.name: No database at launch
providers.recommendation: Preferred for current scope. Versioned calculator registry, formulas and editorial content live in source; calculation state stays in browser memory. Search can use a generated local index.
providers.qualification: Hosting, domain, optional external data feeds, and contact mailbox costs remain separate.

providers.name: Neon Launch / Postgres
providers.recommendation: Preferred future relational option if structured persistence becomes necessary; do not provision speculatively.
providers.billing_timing: Official current pricing page explicitly says metered hourly, billed at end of month; invoices under $0.50 not collected.
notes: Compute scales to zero; retained storage and optional history/snapshots still cost money. No subscription floor is different from no bill for an existing database.
Do not use the older blog compute price of $0.14; current price is $0.106.
Paid plans do not carry the Free plan compute allowance.
Region/provider selection and billing currency should be verified in actual account.
Spending notifications are documented; do not claim they form a hard cap without checking the account feature.

providers.name: Firestore Standard on Firebase Blaze
providers.region: us-central1 (Iowa), default on-demand consumption model, USD, one qualifying default database
providers.billing_timing: Usage-based through Google Cloud Billing; self-serve accounts can use threshold-triggered charges before month-end, not necessarily month-end-only payment.
notes: Read quotas are daily, not a monthly pool. Extra index reads, listeners, security-rule reads, and empty query minimum reads can increase costs.
Stored document metadata/indexes count toward storage.
TTL, backups, restore, PITR have separate paid usage; disabled in sample model.
Australia and China destinations have different egress rates.
Budgets/alerts are not automatic hard stops.

providers.name: Amazon DynamoDB Standard, on-demand
providers.region: us-east-1, single-region Standard table, no provisioned capacity or commitments
providers.billing_timing: Monthly usage billing; AWS normally charges the card on file.
notes: Example unit assumptions: <=4 KiB strongly consistent read = 1 RRU; <=1 KiB write = 1 WRU. Eventually consistent reads use half the units; transactional reads/writes cost more.
25 GB Standard table storage allowance is described on official pricing page; account eligibility and shared consumption must be checked.
Global replicas, backups/PITR, streams/exports, transfer, Lambda/API, and support are separate costs.
Operational/IAM complexity may outweigh savings for this calculator site.

providers.name: Upstash Redis Pay as You Go
providers.recommendation: Possible cache or rate-limit store, not needed for browser calculators.
notes: Paid plan does not inherit free monthly commands.
Writes replicated to additional regions count again; examples assume one primary and no read regions.
First 1 GB storage is free; persistent storage above it costs even without commands.
Optional Prod Pack is $200/month/database and violates a no-fixed-fee choice if enabled.
PAYG supports a hard budget cap implemented through rate limiting; reaching it can affect availability.

providers.name: Cloudflare D1
providers.reason: Free D1 exists, but exceeding free limits requires Workers Paid with a $5/month subscription. D1 usage-only wording does not remove the Workers minimum.
notes: Rows scanned and index maintenance contribute to billing.
D1 itself has no egress fee; Workers execution has its own bill.
Free plan stops queries at daily limits rather than billing overages.

providers.name: Turso Cloud
providers.reason: Free plan exists, but month-to-month Developer tier has a $5.99/month base subscription (annual-discount display $4.99/month). It is not zero-minimum PAYG.

assumptions: These are illustrative request volumes, not measured website traffic forecasts or provider capacity benchmarks. Public browser calculator use generates zero DB reads/writes in the recommended architecture.
30-day month, uniform daily operations, one region, no transactions, no optional paid add-ons, taxes excluded, USD.

Firestore assumes one qualifying default database, direct document reads with a 1 KiB returned payload, no extra index/rules/listener reads, and 30-day hourly storage rate. GB/GiB distinctions are provider-specific; sample stored-size number is interpreted using each provider billing unit.
Firestore sample egress is to US/Europe destinations; other regions and protocol/data overhead can alter bills.
DynamoDB estimates are REQUESTS ONLY with 1 RRU/read and 1 WRU/write; storage allowance eligibility and transfer/service costs are separate.

Neon CU-hours are additional independent assumptions, not inferred from query counts. Actual compute depends on timing, concurrency, indexes, query complexity, and scale-to-zero wake intervals. History, extra branches and snapshots excluded; model egress below 500 GB.
Upstash assumes each operation maps to one billed command, one region, no paid Prod Pack.
Billing alerts are not hard caps unless the provider explicitly enforces one.

braces.guidance: Report the audit finding accurately. If root confirms dev-only dependency, distinguish build/CI exposure from shipped runtime exposure. Do not describe the full audit as clean. Avoid feeding untrusted glob patterns into affected tooling and monitor upstream resolution.
